purpose: Present a dialog task from a chosen viewport edge.
avoid: Edge position does not establish modality or close behavior.
basis: Pinned React/primitive sources lead API, lifecycle and semantics; native visual observations and explicit reference decisions are mapped in figma/traceability.json.
profileRationale: The family presents controls or navigation; static depictions do not establish an interactive contract.
sourceRule: Sheet is a Dialog composition. Content side defaults right and accepts top/right/bottom/left; showCloseButton defaults true. A task commits only through its actual child action; simply closing, Escape or outside press does not invent an application result.
keyboardAndFocus: Sheet inherits the pinned Dialog primitive focus containment, Escape/Close and return-focus behavior. The default modal policy is true; side changes placement, not semantics or commit rules.
referenceDecisions: One stable trigger/content ownership relation per shown instance; concrete labels and task children are caller supplied. Exact wrapper types retain optional handles/payloads/placement overrides. Complete describes this sufficient reference, not a full application/platform certification.

visualContract.layoutPolicy: The pinned Sheet wrapper owns the actual parts and primitive lifecycle; Root/Portal are controllers rather than invented DOM identities. The edge surface follows actual side values; horizontal edge surfaces cap at the selected native 384px width, vertical edge surfaces span the available viewport. Header inset 16px/gap 2px and footer inset 20px/gap 8px retain native section metrics. Native title 16/24 (Medium, or Semi Bold for AlertDialog) and body 14/20 are intrinsic text roles, never fixed frame heights. Footer order remains DOM order and wraps. Button actions explicitly depend on Button tokens/CVA, while primitive triggers remain bare unless the caller composes Button. Backdrop 50% and viewport clearance are explicit reference decisions; static examples do not measure live dimming. Close and Escape follow the actual primitive callback and host authority; no CSS rule invents state transitions.
